strategies.name: Calibrated Elo vs. closing spread
strategies.thesis: Take a side when the calibrated Elo margin disagrees with the closing line by 2+ points. Tests whether a transparent rating is still exploitable against a mature market.

would_change_mind.support: Positive Brier skill against the closing line over a pre-registered forward season (currently -8.1%), with a game-cluster lower bound above zero.
would_change_mind.refute: Another season at the current 51.7% +/- 2.1% hit rate. All 8 gates already failed; only new out-of-sample evidence can revive this.

strategies.name: Fade a team off a 17+ point win
strategies.thesis: Recency bias: the public re-prices a team after a lopsided win. Fade the team that won by 17 or more in its previous game.

would_change_mind.support: A forward sample of 500+ games in which fading 17+ point winners covers 54% or more, with the 95% CI above the 51.5% break-even.
would_change_mind.refute: The current estimate (50.6% +/- 2.8%) persisting: recency bias is already absorbed by the closing line.

strategies.name: Rest differential (3+ days)
strategies.thesis: Extra rest is genuine but usually priced; test whether 3+ days of rest advantage still carries value.

would_change_mind.support: Rest-advantage teams covering 53% or more when the bet is placed before the line fully prices the rest gap (early-week entries only).
would_change_mind.refute: Late-week pricing continuing to absorb rest information before bet time, as the 874-game sample shows.

strategies.name: Six-game scoring pace vs. posted total
strategies.thesis: Both teams' last six games are used to project a total; bet when the projection differs from the posted number by 5+ points, with a wind adjustment.

would_change_mind.support: A pace projection built on verified inputs (availability, opponent-adjusted pace) beating the market total on Brier skill over a forward holdout.
would_change_mind.refute: The six-game window continuing to trail the posted total (47.7% vs 51.6% required): the market's total is the better estimator.

strategies.name: Divisional home underdog
strategies.thesis: Familiarity compresses variance inside a division; test whether the home team in a divisional game priced as a 1+ point underdog covers too often.

would_change_mind.support: Divisional home underdogs covering 54% or more over a forward sample of 400+ games with the lower bound above break-even.
would_change_mind.refute: Variance compression being fully priced inside divisional lines, as the 551-game sample (50.1%) indicates.

strategies.name: Moneyline underdog value
strategies.thesis: Bet the underdog on the moneyline when the model's win probability exceeds the de-vigged market probability by 8+ points. Low hit rate, high payout.

would_change_mind.support: The model's 8+ point probability gaps calibrating: underdogs in that bucket winning at their implied rate plus margin on a forward sample with recorded prices (see decision-readiness DR-01).
would_change_mind.refute: The measured 36.7% hit rate against 38.2% required persisting: the probability gaps would be noise, not miscalibration.

strategies.name: High total + tight spread + calm weather
strategies.thesis: A 47+ total with a spread of 3 or less in calm conditions implies a shootout between evenly matched teams; test the over.

would_change_mind.support: High-total, tight-spread, calm-weather games going over 54% or more on a forward sample of 300+ games.
would_change_mind.refute: The current 50.0% over 374 games persisting: the shootout narrative is already priced in.

strategies.name: Team coming off its bye
strategies.thesis: A team off a bye has two weeks to prepare and is conventionally considered advantaged; test whether it survives as a market edge.

would_change_mind.support: Bye teams covering 53% or more when the line is captured before bye-week practice information is public.
would_change_mind.refute: No residual edge across 413 games (49.6%): two weeks of preparation is priced.

strategies.name: Short-week unders (4 or fewer days rest)
strategies.thesis: Both teams on a short week should have a thinner, less rehearsed game plan; test whether the total is systematically set too high.

would_change_mind.support: Short-week unders hitting 53.5% or more on a forward sample of 200+ short-week games.
would_change_mind.refute: The current 50.0% over 246 games persisting: the market also knows the schedule.

strategies.name: High-wind unders
strategies.thesis: Wind is the weather variable the market handles least well. Test unders when sustained wind is 15+ mph and the total is already 44 or higher.

would_change_mind.support: The 55.1% over 156 games replicating at 54% or more on the next 150 high-wind games with the lower CI above break-even. This is the closest candidate; n is too small to promote.
would_change_mind.refute: Regression to 52% or below on the next 150 high-wind games: the current edge sits inside a +/- 7.9 point noise band.

strategies.name: Fade large weekly line moves
strategies.thesis: Requires an opening-line snapshot for every season. initial_lines.csv covers 2021 only, so the strategy cannot be tested without inventing data.

params.data_gap: No opening-line snapshot outside 2021 in this dataset.

strategies.reason: No opening-line snapshot outside 2021 in this dataset.

would_change_mind.support: A licensed timestamped opening-line feed appearing (see decision-readiness DR-01): the fade-the-move hypothesis then becomes testable under pre-registration.
would_change_mind.refute: Continued absence of opening prices keeps this untestable, which is not evidence for or against the thesis.

gates_definition.requirement: Bootstrap 95% lower bound on hit rate above break-even (52.38% at -110)
Block-bootstrap 95% CI of mean return per bet excludes zero
Model probabilities beat the de-vigged closing line on Brier score
Profitable in at least 60% of evaluated seasons
Survives Benjamini-Hochberg FDR at q = 0.10 across all tested strategies
